anomalies.observed: In the PWM-signal path (top-right of the sheet), the M5Stack bus GPIO nets (NET0004, NET0009 for channel 1; NET0023, NET0003 for channel 2) are connected through 0 Ω jumper resistors (R10, R13, R4, R20) directly to the servo-header signal nodes NET0013 and NET0010, which run straight to J7 pin 1 and J5 pin 1. There is no 1 kΩ series resistor anywhere on the schematic between the jumper outputs and the servo signal pins; the only resistors in the design are the 0 Ω jumpers and the MAX3485 bias network (R1 2k, R18 20k, R24/R5 2.2k) plus the Q3 base divider (R19 10k, R14 5.1k).
anomalies.expected: The specification defines R3 and R4 as 1 kΩ each, in series between the PWM1/PWM2 GPIO nets and the servo-header signal pins (J3 pin 3 / J8 pin 3), i.e. the PWM path should be bus pin -> 0 Ω selection jumper -> 1 kΩ series resistor -> header signal pin, giving each servo an independent 1 kΩ-buffered GPIO line.

anomalies.impact: In PWM mode the SG90-class servo signal lines are driven directly from the M5Stack GPIO through 0 Ω jumpers instead of through the intended 1 kΩ series buffering. This removes the designed current-limiting/edge-damping on the servo control lines, changing signal integrity and protection behaviour relative to the reference design.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the specification (bus pass-through J1/J8, PortB header, battery P-FET switch, external-5V Schottky D3/SS54, servo-rail diode D1/PMEG3030EP with 100 µF bank, MAX3485 with BC857 auto-direction control and bias network, 0 Ω serial/PWM jumpers). However, the 1 kΩ series resistors (R3/R4) that the spec places between the PWM jumper outputs and the servo-header signal pins are absent — the signal nodes connect to the headers through 0 Ω jumpers only — which is a deviation from the intended design.
